bug_description.normalized: On the saved run, `readXCF()` processes at least one visible layer before the later crashing Indexed+Alpha layer; stderr witnesses an earlier visible RGB-layer warning, but the staged artifacts do not uniquely identify whether that specific RGB layer is the one that first initializes `xcf_image.image`. The source-grounded fact is narrower: before the crashing Indexed+Alpha layer reaches `loadLayer()`'s merge path, some earlier visible layer must already have taken the `!xcf_image.initialized` branch, causing `initializeImage()` to create a destination image with depth greater than 8 and `loadLayer()` to leave `xcf_image.initialized = true`. Later, the crashing Indexed+Alpha layer reaches `composeTiles()`, which allocates an Indexed8 `layer.image_tiles` grid plus a separate alpha grid; the saved MSAN origin points at that `layer.image_tiles` allocation at line 845. In the staged vulnerable source, the only project-side write omission on this `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE` path is in `assignImageBytes()`: the indexed image byte is written only under `if (tile[0] < image.colorCount())`, with no fallback assignment when that predicate is false, while the matching alpha byte is still written and processing continues. The saved artifacts do not recover the exact failing palette index or palette size, but this omission is the only source-level path compatible with the later `QImage::pixel()` read from `mergeIndexedAToRGB()` and the saved allocation origin. Because the destination image is already initialized and has depth greater than 8, the later `loadLayer()` invocation takes the merge path and `mergeLayerIntoImage()` selects `mergeIndexedAToRGB()`. That helper then calls `layer.image_tiles[j][i].pixel(k, l)`, and `QImage::pixel()` consumes the untouched indexed byte, producing the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.description: Earlier visible-layer header materialization from the pre-crash prefix. The saved artifacts prove that `readXCF()` reaches at least one visible layer before the later crashing Indexed+Alpha layer, but they do not uniquely identify which earlier visible layer first initializes the destination image.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 44-byte XCF blob beginning with `gimp xcf:`. In the saved vulnerable run, stderr first prints `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 973079040` before the later Indexed+Alpha warning and crash. That warning is emitted only in `loadHierarchy()` for `layer.type == RGB_GIMAGE`, and it sits after the `layer.visible == 0` early return in `loadLayer()`, so at least one earlier visible RGB layer exists on the witnessed path, even though the staged artifacts do not prove that this specific warning layer is the first initializer.
source.note: This earlier layer-header parse is the first source-grounded project materialization point for the pre-crash visible-layer prefix that later leaves `xcf_image.initialized = true` before the crashing merge path.

root_cause.description: Conditional indexed-pixel write with no fallback initialization. If the decoded palette index is not representable in the current palette, the code skips writing the image byte but still writes the alpha byte and continues.
root_cause.note: The saved artifacts do not expose the exact offending `tile[0]` value or `image.colorCount()` on the crashing pixel, but within the staged vulnerable source this is the only `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE` write site that can leave `layer.image_tiles` unwritten while allowing the layer to progress to the later merge sink.

sink.description: Project-side sink callsite. `mergeIndexedAToRGB()` asks Qt to read one indexed pixel from the current layer tile, and `QImage::pixel()` consumes the untouched byte left in `layer.image_tiles`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `QImage::pixel(int, int) const` at `/src/qtbase/src/gui/image/qimage.cpp:2376:13`; frame 1 is this exact line-2642 callsite in `mergeIndexedAToRGB()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: First concrete vulnerability-relevant use of the current indexed pixel. The decoded palette index `tile[0]` is checked against the current palette size and determines whether the destination `layer.image_tiles` byte is initialized at all.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing layer, `tile[0]` comes from the layer's decoded indexed tile data and `image.colorCount()` reflects the palette size installed for `layer.image_tiles[j][i]` in `composeTiles()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved artifacts do not recover the exact pixel index, only that this predicate must evaluate false for at least one later-crashing pixel because the sink reads an uninitialized byte from the same `layer.image_tiles` allocation.

parser_admitted.description: After the XCF tag check succeeds, `readXCF()` materializes the global image header and enters the project XCF parser.
parser_admitted.note: The staged `poc` begins with `gimp xcf:`, so the header gate at lines 325-331 passes and the parser reaches the layer-loading logic below.

coarse_trace.summary: Before the later crashing Indexed+Alpha layer is loaded, some earlier visible layer has already initialized `xcf_image.image` and set `xcf_image.initialized = true`; stderr separately witnesses an earlier visible RGB-layer warning, but not that this specific RGB layer was the initializer.
A later visible Indexed+Alpha layer is decoded, and `composeTiles()` allocates its Indexed8 `image_tiles` / `alpha_tiles`; the `image_tiles` allocation is the MSAN origin.
The Indexed+Alpha tile copy path conditionally skips writing an image byte when the decoded palette index is not representable, leaving that `image_tiles` slot undefined while still writing alpha.

Because some earlier visible layer has already left `xcf_image.initialized = true` and a destination image with depth greater than 8, the later Indexed+Alpha layer goes through `mergeLayerIntoImage()`, and dispatch selects `mergeIndexedAToRGB`.
The merge helper calls `layer.image_tiles[j][i].pixel(k, l)` on the untouched indexed pixel, and Qt reports the saved MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: On an earlier `loadLayer()` invocation from the same witness, this header parse represents the pre-crash visible-layer prefix that precedes the later crashing Indexed+Alpha layer. The saved stderr warning `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 973079040` is emitted only in `loadHierarchy()` for `layer.type == RGB_GIMAGE`, and that warning sits after the `layer.visible == 0` early return, so at least one earlier visible RGB layer is loaded on the witnessed path. The staged artifacts do not, however, uniquely identify whether the earlier visible layer that initializes `xcf_image.image` is that specific RGB warning layer or another earlier visible layer from the same prefix.

`XCFImage` starts with `initialized = false`. Before the later crashing layer reaches line 648, some earlier visible layer must already have executed this block, because the current crashing `loadLayer()` invocation only reaches `mergeLayerIntoImage(xcf_image)` once this earlier path has created the destination image and left `xcf_image.initialized = true`. The saved earlier RGB warning confirms pre-crash visible-layer processing, but the staged artifacts do not uniquely bind the initializing invocation to that warned RGB layer.

fine_trace.note: The exact earlier initializing layer is not recoverable from the staged artifacts, so the source-grounded fact here is narrower: the earlier call to `initializeImage()` must have produced a destination image with `depth() > 8`, because step 8 later executes the `mergeIndexedAToRGB` arm rather than `mergeIndexedAToIndexed`. The saved earlier RGB warning proves one prior RGB layer exists on the witnessed path, but another earlier visible layer could also have been the initializer.

On a later `loadLayer()` invocation from the same XCF, the header parse materializes the crashing layer as `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE`. The saved stderr then prints `Found layer of type Indexed+Alpha but with bpp != 2 973079040`, which comes from `loadHierarchy()` for `layer.type == INDEXEDA_GIMAGE`; because later code allocates tiles and merges this layer, it is visible on the witnessed path.

For the later Indexed+Alpha layer, `composeTiles()` allocates an Indexed8 image tile and a separate Indexed8 alpha tile. The saved MSAN origin stack points to the `layer.image_tiles[j][i] = QImage(...)` allocation at line 845; those image bytes remain uninitialized until `assignImageBytes()` writes them, and `setColorCount(xcf_image.num_colors)` fixes the palette size consulted by the later guard.

Root cause. On the Indexed+Alpha copy path, the image byte is written only when the decoded palette index fits in the current palette. For the crashing pixel, that predicate is false, so `*dataPtr` is skipped and the byte keeps the heap state from step 5; `*alphaPtr = tile[1]` still executes, and the loop advances. The saved artifacts do not recover the exact failing palette index or palette size, but this is the only project-side omission on the witnessed `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE` path that can leave `layer.image_tiles` uninitialized for the later sink.

When the later crashing layer reaches this block, some earlier visible layer has already made `xcf_image.initialized` true, so `loadLayer()` skips the base-image copy path and executes `mergeLayerIntoImage(xcf_image)` at line 648. The saved earlier RGB warning shows one visible earlier layer on this prefix, but the staged artifacts do not uniquely identify which earlier visible layer established the already-initialized destination state. Frame 3 of the saved crash stack is this exact later callsite.

The current layer is `INDEXEDA_GIMAGE`, and the executed `else` arm proves the preexisting destination image has depth greater than 8, so merge dispatch selects `mergeIndexedAToRGB` instead of `mergeIndexedAToIndexed`. Saved stack frames 2 and 1 show that this arm is the one executed on the witness. The staged artifacts do not uniquely identify which earlier visible layer produced that >8-bit destination image.

MSAN sink. The selected RGB merge helper asks Qt to read the current indexed pixel from `layer.image_tiles[j][i]`. For the crashing pixel, step 6 left that byte untouched, so `QImage::pixel()` consumes the uninitialized heap value from step 5 and reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/qtbase/src/gui/image/qimage.cpp:2376:13`.

allocation_context.description: The saved MSAN origin stack points to the Indexed+Alpha image-tile `QImage` allocation in `composeTiles()`. The later bug is not the allocation itself but the conditional skip in `assignImageBytes()` that leaves some of that allocation unwritten.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial. MSAN identifies the `layer.image_tiles` heap allocation in `composeTiles()`, while the logical defect is the later conditional image-byte skip in `assignImageBytes()` that leaves part of that allocation unwritten.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a 44-byte XCF blob beginning with `gimp xcf:`. On the saved vulnerable run, stderr prints `QBuffer::seek: Invalid pos: 1638400`, then `Found layer of type RGB but with bpp != 3 973079040`, then `QBuffer::seek: Invalid pos: 1441792`, then `Found layer of type Indexed+Alpha but with bpp != 2 973079040`, then `QBuffer::seek: Invalid pos: 973079040`, and finally `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `QImage::pixel(int, int) const`. The saved artifacts do not expose the exact offending palette index byte or uniquely identify which earlier visible layer first initialized the later RGB destination. The source-grounded fact is narrower: before the crashing Indexed+Alpha layer reaches merge dispatch, some earlier visible layer has already left `xcf_image.initialized = true` and a destination image with depth greater than 8, and the later Indexed+Alpha layer then hits the conditional image-byte omission recorded in step 6.

format.name: XCF
format.contract: A GIMP XCF byte stream that passes `readXCF()`'s tag check and, on the witnessed path, reaches at least one earlier visible layer before a later visible Indexed+Alpha layer. By the time that later layer reaches `loadLayer()`'s merge path, some earlier visible layer must already have initialized a destination image with `depth() > 8` and set `xcf_image.initialized = true`; the staged artifacts do not uniquely identify which earlier visible layer did so. The later Indexed+Alpha layer must reach `composeTiles()`, and for at least one decoded pixel the vulnerable `assignImageBytes()` guard `tile[0] < image.colorCount()` must be false so the code skips writing `*dataPtr` while still writing the matching alpha byte and continuing. That later layer is then merged through `mergeIndexedAToRGB()`, which reads the untouched indexed byte via `layer.image_tiles[j][i].pixel(k, l)`. The staged evidence establishes this earlier-initialized >8-bit destination plus partial-initialization Indexed+Alpha path, not a broader class of malformed XCF files.
